stage: Frozen after development seeds 1001/1002 and before inspecting any confirmation seed
baseline_selection: Native 1/2/3/4/8 slots and native8 logical batch sizes 64/128/256/512/1024 were evaluated on development only. Native8 batch256 was selected for best interactive P95. simple_cost4 is a thin cost-priority queue outside Lattice without the grace interval.
scope: Synthetic CPU burst: six diverse long-input copy tasks, followed by six short-input copy tasks. Bulk means prefill cost, not sustained long output. No production prevalence or broad competitor claim.
arrival_contract: All arms receive identical absolute-from-origin request offsets and source prompts. End-to-end latency includes intentional grace and queueing. No arrivals wait for completions.
limits_contract: Same pinned model, greedy sampler, 2048-token per-request context, 4096-MiB worker address-space cap, four CPU threads. Actual prompt/output token lengths, EOS, failures, worker and control-plane RSS and dispatch lateness are reported.
quality_gate: Every request has identical token IDs and text to the corresponding native8 request. No exclusion of failures or output-cap finishes.
uncertainty: 10000 seeded hierarchical bootstrap replicates: resample sessions, then whole paired traces within sessions. Latency statistic pools all interactive requests in sampled traces; throughput is sum actual completed tokens divided by sum trace makespans. Report central 95% intervals and raw session/trace results. Three shared-VM sessions are not independent hardware/site replications.
sample_planning: 30 paired traces, 180 interactive requests per arm. This is a fixed-budget confirmation for a large latency effect, not a general tail-SLA study. Throughput gate may remain inconclusive; no optional stopping or added traces after results are inspected.
decision: A pass is restricted to this workload, CPU, model, baseline sweep and configuration. If any gate fails or is inconclusive, do not claim a win and do not relax the gate. Do not call bounded grace or cost-priority scheduling novel algorithms. Default serving policy stays unchanged.
